doc.title: Underwear once a child is fully independent in the bathroom
doc.note: The director's rule. A child is fully independent in the bathroom and tells an educator when they need to go before coming to school in underwear. Until then, a pull-up or diaper. The count of accidents a week comes out.
doc.from: Children may wear underwear when they are reliably toilet trained and have fewer than 3 accidents per week. Daily soiling requires a diaper or pullup.
doc.to: Children wear underwear once they are fully independent in the bathroom and tell an educator when they need to go. Until then, they wear pull-ups or diapers.

doc.title: Underwear once a child is fully independent in the bathroom
doc.note: The director's rule, the same as in Toilet Learning & Diapering. The count of accidents a week comes out.
doc.from: During toilet learning a child wears a diaper or pull-up, a child moves to underwear once reliably toilet trained with fewer than three accidents a week, and daily soiling means a diaper or pull-up.
doc.to: A child comes to school in underwear once they are fully independent in the bathroom and tell an educator when they need to go. Until then, they wear a pull-up or diaper.

doc.title: The LIC 613A link opens the current CDSS form
doc.note: The old CDSS address for the Acknowledgment of Personal Rights no longer opens. The link goes to the current LIC 613A on the CDSS site. Accepting it changes the 2026 edition families read now, and the 2027 draft reads this section from it.

doc.title: The educator looks for the need behind a behavior
doc.note: The educator looks for the need behind a behavior and does not claim to know it for certain. Accepting it changes the 2026 edition families read now. The 2027 draft has its own copy of this section, with its own proposal.
doc.from: The child’s educator will be able to discern the reason for the behaviors the child exhibits, and how to respond to that behavior, in the manner that is most appropriate for the individual child.
doc.to: The child’s educator looks for the need behind a behavior, without claiming to know it for certain, and responds in the way that fits that child.
